sets.assumptions: Ordinary exact ticket prices; the first version presupposes that the two tickets are the adult and child subsequently named.
sets.underlying_facts: One adult and one child ticket total 11 credits, with the adult costing 9 more.
comments: Weak manipulation: plain M004 and trap M022 use almost the same sum-and-difference formulation. Trap wording does not clearly add a new source of linguistic misdirection. Neutral M018 uses combined price and price difference but preserves the algebra.
differences: M004 says two tickets before identifying their types; M018 and M022 identify one of each explicitly.
Neutral nominalizes the difference; plain and trap state the comparative directly.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Average speed means total distance divided by elapsed time. Outbound and return use equal route lengths.
sets.underlying_facts: Two 12 km legs at 6 and 3 km/h with no stops.
comments: The return-trip wrapper changes geography but no relevant numerical information.
Neutral explicitly supplies the definition of average speed; this is a procedural cue, not a changed target or new quantitative fact. Plain and trap both permit the familiar arithmetic-mean error.
differences: M011 uses an out-and-back trip on the same route; M005 and M031 use sequential legs.
M005 asks directly for total distance divided by total time; the others say average speed.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Detected infected devices are members of the flagged group; uniform sampling within that group.
sets.supported_answer: Infection probability among uniformly sampled flagged devices, 9/17 (A).
sets.underlying_facts: 100 total devices, 20 infected, 18 infected flags and 16 uninfected flags.
comments: Equivalent under the ordinary scanner convention that a detection is a flag.

Literal precision qualification: M028 switches from detects to flags without explicitly identifying them. With an artificial distinction between detected and flagged sets the flagged infected count would be missing; M010 and M026 do not require this lexical bridge.
The trap exposes 18/20 as a salient sensitivity fraction. Plain also gives the same numbers; the difference is their framing.
differences: M010 presents the flagged composition directly.
M026 reports scanner flags directly.
M028 phrases infected detections as 18 of 20 before mentioning false-positive flags.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Required is a logical necessary condition, not a policy permitting violations. Unsealed and not sealed are equivalent in this context.
sets.supported_answer: Whether this parcel cannot be sealed; Yes (B).
sets.underlying_facts: Sealed implies labeled; the designated parcel is not labeled.
comments: All three encode the same implication and its contrapositive.
M029 adds genuine polarity-tracking load through no ... lacks and impossible; it does not add a premise.
M015 uses required, which can sound normative outside an abstract logic task. This is a minor wording precision concern under ordinary mathematical reading.
differences: M015 states a necessary condition.
M027 states a direct universal implication and explicitly restricts reasoning to premises.
M029 uses a negated existential and asks about impossibility.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Ordinary seven-day weekday arithmetic with exact relative-day offsets.
sets.underlying_facts: Today is Thursday in every version.
comments: The apparent anchor changes are arithmetically equivalent: Monday three days ago and Tuesday two days ago both fix Thursday today.
Trap wording adds a nested day-after reference and day-before-yesterday offset. Plain and neutral are nearly identical, so their distinction is weak.
differences: M002 and M021 anchor Monday three days before today.
M003 identifies Tuesday indirectly as the day after Monday and places it two days before today.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Token counts are nonnegative; thus the unsigned difference in M017 is Lina minus Omar.
sets.underlying_facts: Lina has twice Omar's count and exceeds it by 6 tokens.
comments: Weak manipulation: all versions directly provide the ratio and difference. M007 compresses them into a relative clause; it is not clearly more misleading than the other versions.
differences: M032 uses two short sentences.
M007 uses which puts her 6 tokens ahead.
M017 uses a nominal unsigned difference, whose direction follows from nonnegative counts.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: The intervention replaces only the X equation and leaves the Y equation in force.
sets.underlying_facts: U=3, initial X=U+2, retained Y=2X+U; X is externally set to 4 with U fixed.
comments: Every version explicitly communicates the intervention override and fixed U. No changed causal information.

Weak manipulation: the trap explicitly says instead of following its equation, while neutral says override only the X equation. Both strongly disambiguate the same operation, so condition separation is slight.
differences: M006 says instead of following its equation.
M020 says override only the X equation.
M024 explicitly leaves both U and the Y equation unchanged.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

sets.assumptions: Each percentage is applied to its explicitly stated base; exact arithmetic.
sets.underlying_facts: Start at 100 credits, reduce by 20%, then increase the reduced amount by 20%.
comments: All versions explicitly identify the reduced-price base for the second percentage.

Weak manipulation: trap M008 adds same percentage, which may prime cancellation, but plain M001 also repeats equal 20% rates. Neutral M009 supplies the equivalent 0.8 multiplier, adding a procedural cue and reducing conversion work.
differences: M001 states both percentages numerically.
M008 calls the rise the same percentage and immediately specifies its base.
M009 replaces the first percentage decrease with multiplication by 0.8.
sets.semantic_equivalence_scope: Relevant mathematical information under ordinary mathematical English; contextual wrappers and procedural cues may differ.

summary.construct_validity_concern: Several wording conditions are weakly separated. These items can test performance on the concrete paraphrases but this review does not validate a general neutral/plain/trap construct or guarantee a manipulation effect.
